title: Cross-Modal Multimodal AI Reasoning Platform Fusing Vision, Speech Audio & Text in PyTorch and FastAPI
problem: Single-modal language and vision models fail catastrophically on tasks requiring joint understanding across disparate sensory inputs, such as visual anomaly inspection guided by spoken technical audio queries. Naively daisy-chaining independent monolithic models produces extreme end-to-end latency, out-of-sync multi-modal context buffers, and cascading transcription errors. This project builds a unified multimodal AI reasoning and retrieval platform in Python and PyTorch. The platform transcribes spoken audio queries using faster-whisper, extracts visual semantics and object embeddings via CLIP, fuses cross-modal representations into unified context vectors, performs multimodal question answering using local quantized vision-language models (LLaVA), and exposes real-time inference endpoints via asynchronous FastAPI.

use_cases.title: Industrial Equipment Maintenance & Visual Inspection
use_cases.first_sentence: Field maintenance engineers inspecting complex factory machinery need to photograph mechanical components while speaking diagnostic questions into headsets.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system fuses the machine photograph with the spoken audio query, identifying equipment wear and returning step-by-step repair guidance within seconds.

use_cases.title: Retail Catalog Product Search & Verification
use_cases.first_sentence: E-commerce shoppers frequently search for products by snapping mobile photos while verbally describing desired color, material, or brand preferences.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine aligns image embeddings with audio transcripts using joint vector projection, searching catalog databases and generating comparative product descriptions.

use_cases.title: Accessibility Assistant for Impaired Document Reading
use_cases.first_sentence: Visually impaired users require assistive tools that process photographed printed documents and answer spoken questions regarding specific passages.
use_cases.second_sentence: The platform analyzes document photos, interprets verbal questions, and synthesizes localized natural language answers grounded strictly in the visual text.

hard_parts: Aligning heterogeneous cross-modal embedding spaces between dense image feature maps (CLIP) and sequential text tokens
Minimizing composite inference pipeline latency across sequential ASR, vision encoding, and autoregressive language generation stages
Implementing graceful degradation and modality dropout handling when image or audio inputs are corrupted or missing
Running multi-model quantized inference (Whisper + CLIP + LLaVA) within 12GB to 16GB consumer GPU VRAM bounds
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating modality encoders, cross-modal attention projection layers, and FastAPI serving endpoints
Comprehensive ablation benchmark demonstrating that joint multimodal reasoning outperforms single-modal vision or text baselines
Anti-fake verification script presenting an unobserved image with an embedded synthetic alphanumeric code and a spoken audio query, verifying correct fused answer generation

architecture.data_flow: The client dispatches an HTTP multipart request containing an image file (JPEG/PNG) and a spoken audio query (WAV); the FastAPI gateway validates file headers and routes payloads in parallel; the Whisper pipeline transcribes the audio into a normalized question string; concurrently, CLIP processes the image into visual feature vectors; the fused context (visual tokens concatenated with prompt text) feeds into the quantized LLaVA vision-language model; LLaVA autoregressively decodes the response, grounding its reasoning in visual evidence; the structured JSON response streams back over HTTP.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Strict image resolution normalization (e.g. 336x336) and audio duration limits (max 30s) preventing out-of-memory GPU panics.

riskiest_component.name: High Cumulative Latency and GPU VRAM Exhaustion Across Sequential Models
riskiest_component.mitigation: Quantize LLaVA weights to 4-bit NF4, execute Whisper and CLIP sequentially to share peak VRAM buffers, and use torch.inference_mode.
riskiest_component.fallback: Offload Whisper speech transcription to CPU and reserve GPU memory exclusively for LLaVA visual generation.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a multimodal reasoning platform in Python/PyTorch fusing Whisper audio and CLIP image embeddings into LLaVA generation with FastAPI.
worksheet.q2: Target users: multimodal AI engineers, computer vision scientists, and applied GenAI platform architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: industrial equipment visual maintenance, retail product catalog search, and accessibility reading assistants.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: cross-modal embedding alignment between CLIP and text tokens, pipeline latency minimization across 3 heavy models, modality dropout resilience, and VRAM management.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 1,000 paired image-audio-text benchmark samples (JPEG images, 16kHz WAV audio, JSON manifests). Public and synthetic data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 16GB RAM, free Colab/Kaggle GPU, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: lightweight CPU models (Moondream/SmolVLM).
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: cumulative latency and VRAM exhaustion. Fallback: 4-bit quantization and sequential execution.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: pre-canned answer lookup. Anti-fake check 5 passes dynamic synthetic barcode image and audio query, asserts exact serial 'SN-9821' in answer.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; public technical equipment photos and synthetic audio recordings only, zero private or biometric data.
